title: The Thiele Machine: No Free Insight
description:
The Thiele Machine is an abstract model of computation. A priced record system has states, moves, a step, a price per move, a reading into an ordered set, and a toll: a move that carries the reading somewhere not at or below where it was costs at least one. A Thiele machine is one whose reading some run raises from a designated start and no move lowers; a flat reading obeys the toll and is a shadow, not a member. The monograph develops the consequences and examples of that definition, the counting that motivates it, and the argument for choosing it. Noninterference is an additional restriction where stated. A ledger sums instruction prices; it need not count only raises.

The book studies retained distinctions, merges or fresh states under a total deterministic rule, observation windows, and the room needed to preserve recoverable histories. Physical interpretations require their stated physical premises; the pointer and physical theses are not presented as theorems.

Version 5.0.0 pairs the reviewed 452-page monograph with the matching tagged repository snapshot. The arguments are in the monograph; the snapshot also carries a formal check of the same statements, a tool for catching mistakes. The publication package consists of both artifacts. The repository includes the monograph source and text, the formal check, and reproduction instructions.
